item.title: Eagles' sudden about-face on IR for Jalen Hurts seems odd, to say the least
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Saturday morning arrived with an ESPN report from its top two insiders regarding the Eagles having no intent to place quarterback Jalen Hurts on IR.
item.content:encoded:
Saturday morning arrived with an ESPN report from its top two insiders regarding the Eagles having no intent to place quarterback Jalen Hurts on IR. Per the article from Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport (who in recent months have morphed from Batman and the Joker into Batman and Robin), the Eagles have "not even discussed the possibility of injured reserve."

Then came 4:00 p.m. ET and the deadline for locking the roster for Week 6. Hurts was placed on injured reserve.

It's unclear what happened between Saturday morning and Saturday afternoon. One more-than-plausible explanation is that the Eagles and Hurts received more medical information, and a possibility that supposedly wasn't even on the radar screen suddenly became the obviously correct destination. The Saturday morning report, however, points to a possible disconnect within the organization as to how the Hurts situation should be handled.

Beyond the odd notion that the Eagles hadn't even considered the possibility of placing a player taking blood thinners to resolve a blood clot on IR, the original article carried hints that the Eagles and Hurts weren't on the same page.

"The ultimate decision about when Hurts returns to play will come from his medical team, and the Eagles are ready to follow his lead," the Saturday morning ESPN report explained. The article also suggested that "some around the team might consider Hurts week-to-week," hours before Hurts was shelved for at least four weeks.

Perhaps the team was still tiptoeing around acknowledging the severity of the situation, given that it allowed him to play last Sunday in London with a blood clot in his leg — and in light of the barest of bare bones disclosure to the public about Hurts's true health condition. Indeed, it's fair to wonder whether the Eagles (and the league) allowed Hurts to play with a blood clot in order to avoid the P.R. mess that would have unfolded if a player who had fully participated in practice all week, who had no injury designation for the game, and who was never downgraded to questionable once the clot was discovered was suddenly scratched from the active roster.

Regardless, the Saturday morning report from ESPN conflicts so sharply with the Saturday afternoon roster move that it invites outsiders to conclude that the team wants everyone to know that the decision to not play Hurts was made by Hurts and his doctors and not by the team.

Either way, Hurts is out for at least the next four games. And possibly longer. The full extent of the absence depends on how long it takes for the clot to be cleared by blood thinners, and whether the situation further deteriorates.

The overriding point is that Hurts has a potentially serious health condition. He was nevertheless permitted to play an entire game with it one week ago. More recently, the team (per the ESPN report) hadn't even entertained the idea of giving him four games to heal.

Whether intended or not, the reporting and the ensuing about-face will make some think the Eagles and Hurts had different ideas on how to best proceed.

item.title: Jalen Hurts will go on injured reserve, miss at least four games and possibly more
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Hurts has a blood clot and will not play until Week 11 at the earliest.
item.content:encoded:
The Eagles will be without starting quarterback Jalen Hurts for at least four games.

Hurts has been placed on injured reserve because of a blood clot, the team announced.

That comes after a previous ESPN report said the Eagles hadn’t even discussed putting Hurts on injured reserve. That seemed hard to believe at the time, and now the team hasn't just discussed it but has done it.

The Eagles' next four games are against the Panthers, Cowboys, Commanders, and Giants, then have their bye. It's possible that Hurts could be back after the bye. But he's currently considered out indefinitely, and it's possible he'll be gone for most or all of the rest of the season. Players who have to go on blood thinners are typically out for more than a month.

The 2-3 Eagles are still contenders in the NFC East, and they'll hope to get Hurts back for a playoff push late in the season. But that's no sure thing.

While Hurts is out, backup quarterback Tanner McKee will start. Rookie Cole Payton is currently McKee's backup, and the recently signed Joe Milton is the No. 3 quarterback in Philadelphia.

item.title: Big 12 admits clock error at end of Notre Dame-BYU game
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Conference pins blame on replay process.
item.content:encoded:
Oops.

That's basically what the Big 12 said after Saturday night's game between Notre Dame and BYU, which resulted in a 28-24 upset of the No. 2 Irish — who surely would have moved to No. 1 with a win, thanks to No. 1 Georgia's loss earlier in the day.

The game ended after a pass by the Irish on first and goal fell incomplete in the end zone. One second remained on the clock. No one noticed it. Not the officials, not the broadcast.

"Following the Big 12's review of the final play of Saturday's Notre Dame-BYU game, it was determined that time remained on the clock when the ball hit the ground and the play was incorrectly cleared by the replay officiating crew," the Big 12 said in a statement. "The Conference will conduct a complete review of its end-of-game officiating process in advance of next week's games."

It's a great gig. Mistakes without consequences. Just say "sorry" and move on.

Last Sunday, referee Ron Torbert was emphatic that one second remained in the Eagles-Jaguars game in London after Jacksonville kick returner Ameer Abdullah was tackled in game-winning field goal range with one second left in overtime. (Which is good, not only because Torbert was right but also because NFL rules prohibit a replay review regarding the time remaining when fewer than two seconds are left on the clock.)

Last night, the referee missed it. The rest of the crew missed it. The replay process — which is there specifically for the purpose of spotting things the on-field officials miss — missed it. Everyone missed it.

Except those who were, you know, watching the game on TV.

Here's the question. Did the replay officials miss it, or did they just say "screw it" because the crowd at LaVell Edwards Stadium had stormed the field? It would have been difficult (but not impossible) to clear the area and resume the game.

The Big 12 statement glosses over explaining how it happened. That's the Occam's razor explanation. If true, that makes the outcome even worse. And, if that's what happened, the "complete review of its end-of-game officiating process" should include permanently relieving whoever made that decision of their duties.

item.title: Jaguars want to play all their home games in Jacksonville when stadium re-opens in 2028
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Jaguars want to stop giving up a home game to play in London when their stadium renovations are complete for the 2028 season.
item.content:encoded:
The Jaguars want to stop giving up a home game to play in London when their stadium renovations are complete for the 2028 season.

Jaguars President Mark Lamping said on Saturday in London, where the Jaguars are playing the Texans on Sunday, that the annual home game at Wembley Stadium should end in 2028, when the renovations in Jacksonville are completed.

“If there’s a natural year where you probably want to play every home game in Jacksonville, it would be the year you open a new stadium,” Lamping said, via the Associated Press.

The Jaguars have played a home game in Wembley every year since 2013.

Construction has started at EverBank Stadium, which has made many seating areas inaccessible and has the Jaguars playing in front of smaller crowds in Jacksonville. Next year, the Jaguars will play most of their home games in Orlando while construction continues.

item.title: Notre Dame gets screwed, twice, on "final" play at BYU
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Home cooking is the best cooking.
item.content:encoded:
Home cooking is the best cooking.

On the final play of BYU's 28-24 home upset of No. 2 Notre Dame, the officials didn't throw a flag for what appeared to be defensive pass interference. Beyond that, one second remained on the clock after the incomplete pass hit the ground.

The clock in the end zone showed one second. The stadium clock showed one second.

Although the DPI non-call was discussed on the broadcast, there was not a single mention of the fact that the game wasn't over after the failed first-and-goal play.

One second remained. Notre Dame should have had one last chance to try to win the game.

It happened six weeks after a controversial decision in Michigan to use replay review to restore time on the clock. In this situation, no effort was made to fix the obvious fact that the game was declared to be over when it was not.

Yes, any team that puts itself in a close game risks being on the wrong side of a screwy outcome. Regardless, Notre Dame got screwed in two different ways on the last play of Saturday night's game.

Which shouldn't have been the last play of the game.

BYU was ahead after 59 minutes and 59 seconds. We'll never know what would have happened if the last second of the game had been played.

item.title: Cowboys downgrade LB Demarvion Overshown to out; Joey Porter Jr. makes trip to Green Bay
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: As expected, Cowboys linebacker DeMarvion Overshown will miss Sunday night's game against the Packers at Lambeau Field.
item.content:encoded:
As expected, Cowboys linebacker DeMarvion Overshown will miss Sunday night's game against the Packers at Lambeau Field.

On Saturday, the Cowboys announced that Overshown, who has a hamstring injury, did not make the trip to Green Bay.

Overshown hasn't played since Week 1. He was listed as questionable; coach Brian Schottenheimer described Overshown as a "long shot" to play. (That would have made him doubtful, but teams don't use that designation as often as they should.)

Also questionable was cornerback Joey Porter Jr., with an ankle injury. He was not downgraded to out, which means he traveled with the team.

Porter played only days after arriving in Dallas, but he missed what would have been his second game due to a sudden illness.

The Cowboys also elevated cornerback Derion Kendrick and safety Juanyeh Thomas from the practice squad. Kendrick becomes insurance, in the event Porter can't play.

item.title: As NFL prepares to stage Steelers-Saints in Paris, local unrest intensifies
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: First-ever game in France is scheduled for October 25.
item.content:encoded:
In little more than a week, the Steelers and Saints will play the NFL's first-ever game in Paris. Although the league recently said it plans to proceed amid persistent local unrest, the situation seems to be getting worse.

On Saturday, more than 1,200 arrests were made after an "escalation in violence" that occurred with roughly 550,000 citizens protesting.

The demonstrations, sparked by concerns regarding conditions in schools and the cost of living, have lingered for weeks.

Said the NFL on Wednesday: “We’re excited for the first-ever regular season game in Paris, and preparations continue as scheduled for NFL events and the game at Stade de France on October 25. As we do for every NFL game, including our international games, we work closely with local authorities and partners on all operational and security matters. We look forward to welcoming fans to Paris later this month.”

If the NFL is going to pivot from Paris to New Orleans (the Saints are the home game for the Week 7 contest), a decision may need to be made soon.

Obviously, the NFL has a very strong interest in following through with all of its international games. Then there's the fact that the game is set for a 9:30 a.m. ET standalone broadcast window on NFL Network.

When the Chiefs-Rams game moved from Mexico City to L.A. in 2018 due to poor field conditions, the time for the game (Monday night) didn't change. If the NFL pulls the plug on the Paris game and plays in New Orleans, would the game begin at 9:30 a.m. ET?

It's also possible, in theory, to play the Steelers-Saints game in London, if either Tottenham Hotspur Stadium or Wembley Stadium are available. Either way, any change in location would become a potential logistical nightmare for the NFL, the teams, and the fans that have made plans to travel to France.

That outcome is still better than having NFL personnel, team personnel, or NFL fans caught in the middle of the mess that continues to play out in Paris.

item.title: Aqib Talib tees off on Ryan Fitzpatrick for his comments about Bo Nix
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Four years ago, Aqib Talib and Ryan Fitzpatrick were scheduled to become colleagues on Prime Video's coverage of Thursday Night Football.
item.content:encoded:
Four years ago, Aqib Talib and Ryan Fitzpatrick were scheduled to become colleagues on Prime Video's coverage of Thursday Night Football. If Talib hadn't stepped aside from the job after his brother shot and killed a man at a youth football game, the most recent postgame show could have gotten very spicy.

After Thursday nights 17-14 overtime win by the Broncos over the Seahawks, Fitzpatrick went all in as to Broncos quarterback Bo Nix. Fitzpatrick called Nix's performance "almost disrespectful to the quarterback position" before later saying, "That right there is garbage. That effort is garbage."

It felt personal or, frankly, planted by someone from the Broncos in an effort to send a message to Nix. Either way, it was over the top. And it has prompted a reaction from Talib, whose career included a stint with the Broncos.

“You are disrespectful to the quarterback position because you suck," Talib said on the Gridiron podcast. "Period."

Talib had plenty more to say about Fitzpatrick.

"We’re talking about a guy who played for nine different teams in 17 years," Talib added. "Ain’t nobody want his ass. We’re talking about a guy who only played for a team for more than two years once. That’s Buffalo. And his record as a starter in Buffalo was 19-35. That’s fucking suck. A guy who played 17 years, 147 starts, and never sniffed a playoff game. He never touched the playoffs ever. That’s disrespectful to the quarterback position.

"You suck. You suck, bro. We’re talking about a guy who got 169 interceptions, more interceptions than he has starts. How can a quarterback of his caliber talk about what is disrespectful to the quarterback position? I know Amazon is begging for you to be more entertaining, and you've just got to just blabber out some bullshit. Nobody’s worried about what Fitzpatrick said. Nobody was worried about playing against you. You suck.”

It's a harsh, blunt critique from Talib. But it's not much more harsh or blunt than what Fitzpatrick said about Nix. And it will be interesting to see whether Fitzpatrick has anything to say in response to Talib.

item.title: After overcoming severe colitis in 2024, Auburn's Alex McPherson kicks game-winner vs. No. 1 Georgia
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Evan McPherson is in his sixth season as the kicker of the Cincinnati Bengals.
item.content:encoded:
Evan McPherson is in his sixth season as the kicker of the Cincinnati Bengals. His younger brother, Alex, is doing the family business proud.

Alex McPherson kicked a 34-yard field goal as time expired, vaulting unranked Auburn to a 27-24 win over No. 1 Georgia. It's the second straight weekend in which the No. 1 team lost to an unranked foe, after Oklahoma defeated No. 1 Texas last Saturday.

Auburn was an 18.5-point underdog for the game played in Athens, Georgia.

Alex McPherson's personal story makes his achievement far more noteworthy. In 2024, a bout with severe ulcerative colitis and Crohn’s disease resulted in the removal of his entire large intestine.

“That week I began to feel sick, I would run to the bathroom 15-20 times a day," Alex McPherson said last year. "I thought I just had the flu or a stomach bug or something going on. My weight was down. I had lost 20 pounds.”

He eventually lost 55 pounds. When he was admitted to the hospital, he weighed 110 pounds.

He's now back to full health. In high school, Alex kicked a 61-yard field goal.

“It’s been really fun, really excited just to be back to normal from where I was,” Alex McPherson said at the SEC Media Days in July 2026. “Just to have that strength back to kind of kick how I want to and how I used to. I think I’m kicking as good as I have since before I got sick and it’s just really exciting to be able to do that and play with the guys to the full extent.”

Alex McPherson is in his final year at Auburn. Come 2027, he could be joining his big brother in the NFL. It's an outcome that would have been inconceivable two years ago.

item.title: Steve Sarkisian doesn't rule out benching Arch Manning
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The 2026 season for the University of Texas is quickly imploding.
item.content:encoded:
The 2026 season for the University of Texas is quickly imploding. And it could result in the benching of quarterback Arch Manning.

Via Danny Davis of the Austin American-Statesman, Longhorns coach Steve Sarkisian opened the door to replacing Manning after Saturday's 27-24 loss to Florida.

Asked whether Sarkisian considered making a change at quarterback, he said, "I just felt like we didn't play good offensive football and we're not playing great offensive football right now. So everything is going to be evaluated."

Sarkisian then was asked whether that means his starting quarterback.

"Everything means everything," Sarkisian replied.

If K.J. Lacey replaces Manning, the college career of Peyton and Eli's nephew would be thrown for a loop. Not long ago, Arch was the betting favorite to be the first overall pick in the 2027 draft. If Sarkisian removes Manning from the lineup, he'd likely take another year before joining the NFL — possibly after transferring to a new program.

Against Florida, Manning struggled. Last week, a pair of fourth-quarter interceptions in the Red River Rivalry set the stage for the first Texas loss of the season, 27-24 to Oklahoma. Next week, Texas hosts Mississippi.

Carrying the Manning name is equal parts blessing and curse. It has allowed Arch to earn millions in NIL payments. It also has invited significant scrutiny and the creation of a high bar that he's currently falling far short of meeting.

Fullback Kyle Juszczyk is set to return to the 49ers' lineup on Monday night.

Juszczyk missed last Sunday's win over the Seahawks with a knee injury, but was up to full practice participation on Saturday. The team did not give him an injury designation for their home game against the Commanders.

Wide receiver Mike Evans (ribs, Achilles) is listed as questionable to play. Evans did not practice this week, but the 49ers are leaving the door open for him to play.

Defensive end Nick Bosa (knee, calf), wide receiver Deebo Samuel (hamstring), safety Marques Sigle (ankle), and linebacker Garret Wallow (hamstring) have been ruled out. Defensive tackle Gracen Halton (quad), wide receiver Christian Kirk (calf), safety Siran Neal (neck), cornerback Upton Stout (shoulder), and defensive end Mykel Williams (knee) are all listed as questionable.

item.title: Bill Belichick beats Duke for the first time, as North Carolina wins in Durham
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Bill Belichick has claimed that the first words he ever spoke were "Beat Duke," because his father was an assistant coach at North Carolina.
item.content:encoded:
Bill Belichick has claimed that the first words he ever spoke were "Beat Duke," because his father was an assistant coach at North Carolina. Now, a Belichick has beaten Duke for the first time.

Belichick's North Carolina team beat Duke today, 24-20, blowing a 17-0 lead, falling behind 20-17 and then coming back with the game-winning touchdown with less than two minutes remaining.

In Belichick's first season at North Carolina last year, his Tar Heels lost to Duke. And North Carolina went 0-3 against Duke in the three years that Belichick's father, Steve Belichick, was a Tar Heels assistant. So this win was special for Belichick.

It's also special because it's more evidence that Belichick is turning things around after his disappointing debut season. The Tar Heels are now 4-2 after finishing 4-8 last year.

Whether Belichick can turn North Carolina into a college football power remains to be seen, but he has his team heading in the right direction, with a big win over a big rival today.

item.title: Will Troy Aikman finish the season with Monday Night Football?
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Because millions care intensely about NFL football, they have similarly strong feelings about the voices that narrate the action on TV.
item.content:encoded:
Because millions care intensely about NFL football, they have similarly strong feelings about the voices that narrate the action on TV. And the unexpected escalation of tensions between Troy Aikman and ESPN/ABC has plenty of people wondering whether the relationship will end before his current contract expires.

Boomer Esiason raised the question this week on his WFAN morning show of whether Aikman would walk away.

“I don’t think he would do it, that’s not his nature, I don’t think," Esiason said Friday, via Brandon Contes of Awful Announcing.

Of course, it may not be Aikman's choice. ESPN could yank him from the broadcast whenever it chooses, if the situation continues to deteriorate. Sure, they'd need to replace him on the fly. But they currently have a small army of NFL voices on the payroll — many of whom would drive a lawnmower through a minefield for a chance to fill the spot.

It's hard to imagine Aikman walking away in a Super Bowl year. But if he becomes sufficiently disillusioned with the situation, it can't be ruled out.

Much of it depends on whether any of the apparent animosity makes its way into a broadcast. For now, it hasn't. But everyone who's aware of the situation (and, frankly, many who watch Monday Night Football aren't and won't be) will be watching and listening for any hint in any stray comment or pointed remark.

Ultimately, it takes two to tango in any employment relationship. And if the two sides know the music will stop once the confetti falls in L.A. on Valentine's Day, a premature record scratch is possible.

In some respects, it's already happening.

item.title: Bradley Chubb fined for taunting Alaric Jackson before Jackson punched him
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Bills linebacker Bradley Chubb did not retaliate physically after Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson punched him in the aftermath of Buffalo's Week 5 win in Los Angeles, but he did get disciplined by the league for his part in the altercation.
item.content:encoded:
Bills linebacker Bradley Chubb did not retaliate physically after Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson punched him in the aftermath of Buffalo's Week 5 win in Los Angeles, but he did get disciplined by the league for his part in the altercation.

The NFL announced on Saturday that Chubb has been fined $14,239 for taunting Jackson before Jackson took a swing at him. Chubb acknowledged that he initiated the interaction between the two men.

Jackson was suspended two games for his actions, but the ban was reduced to one game after he appealed the punishment. He will lose $934,555 while sitting out Sunday's game against the Cardinals.

Bills running back James Cook was fined $21,167 for illegal use of the helmet and safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson was fined $11,194 for unnecessary roughness. Rams defensive lineman Braden Fiske was fined $11,941 for a facemask foul.

item.title: Reports: Caleb Williams to start for Bears Sunday
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Bears quarterback Caleb Williams was coy about his availability for Sunday's game against the Falcons during a Friday press conference, but he seemed to send a message with a social media post later in the day.
item.content:encoded:
Bears quarterback Caleb Williams was coy about his availability for Sunday's game against the Falcons during a Friday press conference, but he seemed to send a message with a social media post later in the day.

Williams posted a video that strongly suggested he would be returning from the hamstring injury that caused him to miss the last three weeks and multiple reports on Saturday afternoon confirm that is the case. Williams is set to start for the 3-2 Bears against the 2-3 Falcons.

Williams was a full participant in practice all week, but the Bears listed him as questionable on Friday.

The Bears won the first two games that Williams missed, but they struggled with Tyson Bagent at quarterback in last Sunday's loss to the Packers.

item.content:encoded:

Running back Jaydon Blue has been signed off of the practice squad. Blue signed with the Eagles after being cut by the Cowboys at the end of the summer.

Blue was a fifth-round pick in Dallas in 2025. He had 38 carries for 129 yards and a touchdown in five appearances during his rookie season.

With Saquon Barkley ruled out and two other backs on injured reserve, Blue will join Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele as the available running backs against the Panthers on Sunday.

The Eagles also announced that they have elevated linebacker Keyshawn James-Newby and safety Cole Wisniewski from the practice squad for Sunday's game.

item.title: Minkah Fitzpatrick, five others fined for player safety fouls in Week 6
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The NFL confirmed that Jets safety Minkah Fitzpatrick was fined for his hit on a defenseless KC Concepcion in the Jets' Week 5 win over the Browns and they announced five other players were fined for the player safety fouls that count toward potential suspensions.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL confirmed that Jets safety Minkah Fitzpatrick was fined for his hit on a defenseless KC Concepcion in the Jets' Week 5 win over the Browns and they announced five other players were fined for the player safety fouls that count toward potential suspensions.

Fitzpatrick said this week that he plans to appeal the $17,911 fine for the hit, which knocked Concepcion out of the game with a concussion. Concepcion has cleared concussion protocol and is set to play against the Ravens in Week 6.

Fitzpatrick was also fined $11,941 for tackling Concepcion by the facemask earlier in the game.

Colts linebacker Austin Ajiake and 49ers safety Malik Mustapha were also fined for hits on defenseless players. Ajiake's fine was $5,583 and Mustapha's was $6,998.

Ravens defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike ($17,911), Lions defensive end D.J. Wonnum ($12,611), and Titans cornerback Micah Robinson ($5,583) were all fined for hip-drop tackles.

It is the first infraction for each player. Any player who is fined three times for one of five player safety rules — horse-collar tackles, launching and blindside blocks are the others — is subject to a one-game suspension.

item.title: The "black box" idea could be adopted by some teams
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: In the aftermath of the Commanders' overtime clock debacle against the Giants, it became impossible to figure out exactly what had happened.
item.content:encoded:
In the aftermath of the Commanders' overtime clock debacle against the Giants, it became impossible to figure out exactly what had happened. Especially with everyone involved taking the blame for it.

A reader had an idea that was good enough to steal and use: Teams should record and preserve all communications, like the "black box" on an airplane.

We floated that concept, and at least someone was listening.

“Yeah, it’s chaos,” an unnamed head coach told Albert Breer of SI. “The coordinator’s gotta have discipline. I mean, it is fucking chaos. It’s like, 'Everyone, shut the fuck up.' Florio had a good one — they should black box the headsets. You could make a movie off of that shit."

Maybe some teams already do it; if they do, they don't advertise it. And those who may start doing it likely won't make the communications available to the public.

Still, it's critical for internal purposes. How can ownership (other than Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon, who puts herself in the fray for precisely such seasons) know what truly happened when left to the inherent flaws of human memory, especially when things are happening in a chaotic environment and when human nature will prompt some to slip into a CYA posture?

It can't be difficult to save the conversations, and it wouldn't be expensive. As we learned on Sunday, it's necessary to knowing how a strange situation unfolded. That knowledge could go a long way toward figuring out who has the true responsibility for the ensuing snafu, and how to best prevent it from happening again.

item.content:encoded:
The Commanders played without wide receiver Stefon Diggs last Sunday and they'll wait to make a call on his availability for Monday's game against the 49ers.

Diggs has been listed as questionable to play after practicing on a limited basis the last two days. Diggs, who had 18 catches in the first four games, has been battling a hamstring injury.

The Commanders listed eight other players as questionable as well. The group includes cornerback Trey Amos (ankle), linebacker Jordan Magee (hamstring), and running back Jeremy McNichols (quad). All three players would need to be activated in order to play in Week 6.

Safety Percy Butler (hamstring), safety Nick Cross (illness), defensive tackle Javon Kinlaw (ankle, knee), safety Tyler Owens (hamstring), and offensive lineman Lucas Patrick (illness) are the other questionable players on the active roster.

Head coach Dan Quinn announced earlier on Saturday that running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin), linebacker Javontae Jean-Baptiste (pectoral), quarterback Marcus Mariota (knee), and defensive end Charles Omenihu (groin, ankle) will not play.

item.title: Grant Delpit sums up difference between Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley in four words
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: On Sunday, Ravens quarterback Tyler Huntley will make his 19th career NFL start (including playoffs).
item.content:encoded:
On Sunday, Ravens quarterback Tyler Huntley will make his 19th career NFL start (including playoffs). For the Ravens, he's 6-7 with three straight wins.

On Friday, Browns safety Grant Delpit addressed some of the similarities between Huntley and two-time MVP Lamar Jackson. Delpit then was asked to identify the biggest difference.

"One is Lamar Jackson," Delpit said.

He's right. But Huntley has proven to be capable. Last week, he completed 24 of 32 passes for 201 yards, two touchdowns, and no interceptions. He added 20 rushing yards and a touchdown on the ground.

So while he's not Lamar (no one is), Huntley can do enough. Delpit's acknowledgement of the obvious could give Huntley a little extra incentive to prove that the gap may not be quite as large as Delpit thinks.

The stakes are high. A win by Cleveland (which would be their fourth straight in the AFC North, a first since 1987) would tie the Ravens and Browns at 4-2. A loss would give Baltimore a two-game lead over the Browns and the first half of the head-to-head tiebreaker.

item.title: Arch Manning struggles and Colin Simmons is carted as Texas loses to Florida
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Formerly No. 1 Texas lost its second straight game on Saturday, and it was a particularly rough day for the Longhorns' two highest-profile 2027 NFL draft prospects.
item.content:encoded:
Formerly No. 1 Texas lost its second straight game on Saturday, and it was a particularly rough day for the Longhorns' two highest-profile 2027 NFL draft prospects.

Texas quarterback Arch Manning, who until recently was the betting favorite to go first overall in next year's draft, had another bad game. Manning had been up and down throughout, but when Texas got the ball back down by three with two and a half minutes to play, it looked like an opportunity for Manning to engineer a great comeback. Instead, Manning was sacked and fumbled, Florida recovered, and that was that. Florida won, 27-24.

The other top draft prospect on the Longhorns, Texas pass rusher Colin Simmons, the NCAA leader in sacks and a potential Top 5 pick in 2027, was carted off with a left leg injury in the fourth quarter.

Manning has been known to make big plays with his legs at times, but he couldn't do that today against Florida. In one particularly rough sequence, Manning attempted to run for a first down on third-and-1 but lost a yard. Texas then went for it on fourth-and-2, Manning again tried to run, and he again was tackled behind the line of scrimmage for a turnover on downs. He also repeatedly failed to escape pass pressure.

Florida running back Jadan Baugh, considered by some the best running back prospect in the 2027 draft class, scored the fourth-quarter winning touchdown for the Gators. He finished with 25 carries for 91 yards.

But the story of the game will be Manning, who has failed to live up to the hype. This was an ugly performance, following an ugly performance in last week's loss to Oklahoma, and it's fair to question whether Manning is a future NFL star, or whether he just shares the same last name as three past NFL stars.

item.title: Sean McVay believes the Harrison Mevis blocked field goal would have missed anyway
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: After Monday night's overtime loss to the Bills, Rams coach Sean McVay minced no words — he said the field goal unit lost the game.
item.content:encoded:
After Monday night's overtime loss to the Bills, Rams coach Sean McVay minced no words — he said the field goal unit lost the game.

The next day, kicker Harrison Mevis lost his roster spot.

And it wasn't just that the potential game-winning field goal from 48 yards was blocked. McVay believes, even without the effort from Gregory Rousseau to get a hand on the ball, the kick would have missed.

“I didn't think it would have gone in, I did not," McVay told reporters on Friday. "I could be wrong, but it didn't look like the trajectory was on alignment.”

If so, the block straightened it out. And it nearly had enough distance to clear the crossbar.

With Mevis gone, Blake Grupe takes over.

"He has a nice demeanor about himself," McVay said regarding the team's new kicker. "There's a quiet confidence, but a humility that you want. I'm looking forward to seeing him produce and then I think it's part of our job to put him in positions that have successful outcomes. Ideally, it's more extra points than anything else."

Still, Grupe's range (his career long is 60 yards) gives the team a broader window for attempting field goals.

“I think having a strong leg is attractive, especially like at the end of a half or at the end of the game," special-teams coordinator Bubba Ventrone told reporters. "You need the range to be able to do so and to be able to hit it with accuracy. I think he's done a good job in his career to be able to do that. He gets good elevation on his kicks. He has a strong leg despite his size. He is an explosive guy. I really am excited to work with him.”

Elevation is a key factor. Mevis wasn't able to get the ball over Rousseau's hand. Even if it had, McVay thinks it would have missed the mark.

item.title: Jaguars look to match best six-game start in team history
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: As the Jaguars prepare to play their second straight game in London, they have an opportunity to do something they haven't done in 27 years — start the year 5-1.
item.content:encoded:
As the Jaguars prepare to play their second straight game in London, they have an opportunity to do something they haven't done in 27 years — start the year 5-1.

The Jaguars last started 5-1 in 1999. That year, they finished 14-2 and lost in the AFC Championship, to the Titans.

This year, Jacksonville has a chance (thanks to the division it's in) to win enough games to secure the No. 1 seed. The next test is a big one, however.

The Texans have done well against the Jaguars in recent years. Quarterback Trevor Lawrence has a 3-7 record against the Texans, with eight touchdown passes and 11 interceptions in those games. Via NBC Sports research, no player since Lawrence's rookie season has thrown more interceptions against a single opponent than Lawrence against the Texans.

The Texans, meanwhile, have a 15-5 record in division games since DeMeco Ryans became the head coach. In those games, quarterback C.J. Stroud has a record of 12-5, with 24 touchdown passes and five interceptions.

item.content:encoded:
Bears General Manager Ryan Poles said in September that he didn't know if cornerback Kyler Gordon would play for the Bears again, but it looks like he'll be back in their lineup against the Falcons on Sunday.

item.title: College football player Tyler Ulrich dies five days after suffering traumatic injury during a game
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Tyler Ulrich, a 21-year-old football player at Southern Nazarene University, died Thursday.
item.content:encoded:
Tyler Ulrich, a 21-year-old football player at Southern Nazarene University, died Thursday. He had suffered a traumatic injury five days earlier.

The injury happened in a game against Ouachita Baptist University in Arkansas.

There are no details about the injury suffered by Ulrich, who played safety at SNU. Via KOCO, the Southern Nazarene play-by-play announcer Dave Myrick said Ulrich was down on the field after the play, but that he couldn’t tell what had happened.

It's an unimaginable tragedy for Ulrich's family and his team. Saturday's game at Southwestern State University has been canceled.

A GoFundMe account has been established to assist Tyler's family during this time.

We extend our condolences to Tyler Ulrich's family, teammates, coaches, and friends.
